items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor Freeman opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which many of us are gathered today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishnaabe and Neutral peoples. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous people with whom we share this land today.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Councillor Freeman provided Council with a moment of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

items.title: Disclosure of Pecuniary Interest and the General Nature Thereof
notes: No disclosure of pecuniary interest was declared by any member of Council at this point in the meeting.

items.title: Community Justice Centre
notes: Chris Cowie, Executive Director, Community Justice Initiatives Waterloo Region spoke about the work of the Community Justice Initiatives, including their work on restorative justice and crime prevention through upstream initiatives. Jason Spencer, Program Director, Community Justice Initiatives Waterloo Region spoke about the work they’re doing at the Community Justice Centre. They then responded to questions of Council.

motions.text: 1. That Council approve IPPW2024-013. 2. motions.text: 1. That CAO2024-009 be approved. 2. That Council approves the phasing of the approved Tax Increment Grant to Reid’s Heritage Homes Ltd. for the property known as 119 Roger Street, previously approved via report CAO2019-029. 3. That the joint phased Tax Increment Grant does not exceed the maximum amount of $728,954 for the City for the Initial Registration Phase to be financed from the incremental tax revenue for the property following remediation, redevelopment and reassessment. 4. That the joint phased Tax Increment Grant does not exceed the maximum amount of $392,820 for the City for Phase One be financed from the incremental tax revenue for the property following remediation, redevelopment and reassessment. 5. That the joint phased Tax Increment Grant does not exceed the maximum amount of $119,415 for the City for Phase Two be financed from the incremental tax revenue for the property following remediation, redevelopment and reassessment. 6. That the Region of Waterloo brownfield coordinator be advised of City Council’s decision regarding this application. 7. That the Mayor and Clerk be authorized to execute Phased TIG Agreements, and any related documents, in coordination with the Region of Waterloo with the registered owner of 119 Roger Street to the satisfaction of the City and Regional Solicitors.
motions.text_html:
1. That CAO2024-009 be approved.

2. That Council approves the phasing of the approved Tax Increment Grant to Reid’s Heritage Homes Ltd. for the property known as 119 Roger Street, previously approved via report CAO2019-029.

3. That the joint phased Tax Increment Grant does not exceed the maximum amount of $728,954 for the City for the Initial Registration Phase to be financed from the incremental tax revenue for the property following remediation, redevelopment and reassessment.

4. That the joint phased Tax Increment Grant does not exceed the maximum amount of $392,820 for the City for Phase One be financed from the incremental tax revenue for the property following remediation, redevelopment and reassessment.

5. That the joint phased Tax Increment Grant does not exceed the maximum amount of $119,415 for the City for Phase Two be financed from the incremental tax revenue for the property following remediation, redevelopment and reassessment.

6. That the Region of Waterloo brownfield coordinator be advised of City Council’s decision regarding this application.

7. That the Mayor and Clerk be authorized to execute Phased TIG Agreements, and any related documents, in coordination with the Region of Waterloo with the registered owner of 119 Roger Street to the satisfaction of the City and Regional Solicitors.
